last_3_hypotheses: Agent-as-judge novelty scoring only tracks human judges meaningfully above κ = 0.6 inter-rater agreement; below that, the agent's signal is dominated by its own prior.
Cron-installed SLA sweeps fire at the expected 15-minute cadence as long as the system clock has not drifted more than 30s from UTC.
BGE-M3 embedding latency rises sub-linearly with batch size up to ~32, then flattens because the model's attention is dominated by the longest sequence in the batch.
proposed_hypothesis_text: For ordinal-tier novelty judgments, Spearman rank correlation between agent and human is a more informative agreement metric than Cohen's κ — κ over-penalizes tier-adjacent disagreements that Spearman treats as near-ties.
rationale: Both touch the same evaluator (agent-as-judge novelty) and both involve agreement statistics. But the prior hypothesis names a κ threshold for credibility; the proposed argues κ is the wrong metric. These are not duplicates — the proposed could falsify the prior. A meta-reviewer that conflates "talks about κ" with "makes the same claim" would mis-route this.
